title: Ensure Default Configuration Passwords Have Been Changed
description: All default/sample passwords must be changed before production deployment: scheduler.xml: oc_tool password, system user passwords oss.json: system accounts (tdsqlsys_kp_new, tdsqlsys_check, tdsqlsys_agent, tdsqlsys_repl, tdsqlsys_normal) ZooKeeper authentication credentials MySQL root and administrative user passwords
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6 Ensure Default Configuration Passwords Have Been Changed

audit.command: Run grep -rE 'password\s*=\s*"(root|admin|123456|password|test)"' <tdsql>/conf/ (must return nothing) and grep -E "password|pwd" <tdsql>/conf/scheduler.xml: values must be long encrypted strings. Diff the password fields of the installed scheduler.xml against the install template; any value equal to the template sample value is a finding.

remediation.command: Change all default passwords and use TDSQL's encrypted storage capability: <!-- Use a strong, encrypted password --> <oc_tool location="/data/oc_agent/bin" port="8966" user="tdsql" password=" <encrypted_strong_password>" /> TDSQL provides a password encryption utility for offline password encryption.

title: Ensure `skip-grant-tables` Is Disabled
description: When MySQL is started with --skip-grant-tables, the server does not load the privilege system, and any user can log in without authentication and perform arbitrary operations. Counts mysqld processes started with --skip-grant-tables and my.cnf files (/data/tdsql/mysqld/*/my.cnf, /etc/my.cnf) that enable it.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Ensure `skip-grant-tables` Is Disabled

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep mysqld | grep -ci '[s]kip.grant.tables' || true); c=$(grep -il '^[[:space:]]*[s]kip.grant.tables' /data/tdsql/mysqld/*/my.cnf /etc/my.cnf 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo $((p + c))

remediation.command: Remove skip-grant-tables from my.cnf and the mysqld command line and restart the MySQL instance.

title: Ensure Authentication Is Enabled on the OSS Management Platform
description: The TDSQL OSS management platform provides API authentication, supporting username/password- and token-based authentication as well as IP allowlisting. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql); reads <TDSQL_HOME>/conf/scheduler.xml and passes when <oss_auth> has enable="1". Also confirm pwd_strength="2" and expire_hours of 24 or less.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.8 Ensure Authentication Is Enabled on the OSS Management Platform

audit.command: f="${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/conf/scheduler.xml"; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1; if grep -Eo '<oss_auth[^>]*' "$f" | grep -Eq '[[:space:]]enable="1"'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Set <oss_auth enable="1" ... pwd_strength="2" expire_hours="24" enable_token_renewal="1" /> in scheduler.xml and restart OSS.

title: Ensure the OSS Super User Password Has Been Changed
description: The OSS management platform includes a built-in super user (osssuper) for initialization and emergency management operations.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.9 Ensure the OSS Super User Password Has Been Changed

audit.command: Check <super_user username="osssuper" pwd="..."> in <tdsql>/conf/scheduler.xml: the pwd value must be in encrypted form (a long base64/ciphertext string) and must differ from the install template (diff <(grep super_user <installed>/conf/scheduler.xml) <(grep super_user <template>/scheduler.xml)). The template sample value is a finding.

remediation.command: 1. Change the super user password to a strong random value (16+ characters including uppercase, lowercase, digits, and special characters) and store it encrypted with the cluster master key. 2. Enable automatic password rotation (rotation="1"). 3. Restrict the super user's source IP (set the host field to a specific IP range, avoiding %).

title: Ensure ZooKeeper Authentication Credentials Have Been Changed
description: TDSQL uses digest authentication to connect to ZooKeeper. The initial credentials used during installation should be uniformly changed to strong random values by the deployment side before production and stored encrypted.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 11.2 Ensure ZooKeeper Authentication Credentials Have Been Changed

audit.command: # 1. Attempt to access a key ZNode via zkCli as an unauthorized identity (should be denied) zkCli.sh -server <zk_ip>:<port> ls /tdsql # Expected: Authentication is not valid # 2. Compare the deployed ZK authentication credentials against the install template's initial values; they must differ # (The exact location depends on the deployment form: centralized deployment uses scheduler.xml; TCE deployment uses the tdsql_install template)

remediation.command: 1. Generate a new strong random password (>= 16 characters including uppercase, lowercase, digits, and special characters). 2. Batch-update the ZK authentication configuration of all TDSQL components (OSS, Manager, Scheduler, Keeper, Agent, Proxy) via the deployment tool. 3. Re-setAcl existing ZNodes to apply the new credentials. 4. Enable ACL mode (see Recommendation 10.1). Note: This operation requires updating all components simultaneously;

title: Ensure a Dedicated Least-Privilege Account Is Used for TDSQL Processes
description: Each TDSQL component (OSS, Manager/Scheduler/Keeper, Agent, MySQL) should run under a dedicated, non-root, least-privilege operating system account. The MySQL daemon should not run as root. TDSQL management processes should run under a dedicated account (e.g., tdsql). Counts mysqld, oss_server, scheduler and ZooKeeper processes running as root (FAIL when none of these processes is running).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure a Dedicated Least-Privilege Account Is Used for TDSQL Processes

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,comm=,args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2 ~ /^(mysqld|mysqld_safe|oss_server|scheduler)$/ || ($2 == "java" && /zookeeper/) {n++; if ($1 == "root") r++} END {if (n == 0) exit 1; print r + 0}'

remediation.command: Create a dedicated system account (groupadd -r tdsql; useradd -r -g tdsql -s /sbin/nologin -d /data/tdsql tdsql), chown the TDSQL directories to it and restart each component under that account.

title: Ensure MYSQL_PWD and Sensitive Environment Variables Are Not Used
description: The MYSQL_PWD environment variable stores the MySQL password in cleartext. Any environment variable used to pass runtime passwords or encryption keys should not persist in the process environment on production nodes. Counts running processes whose environment contains MYSQL_PWD plus system and user shell profiles that set it (run as root to read every /proc/<pid>/environ). Also review environments for other *_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variables.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure MYSQL_PWD and Sensitive Environment Variables Are Not Used

audit.command: c=$( { grep -l MYSQL_PWD /proc/[0-9]*/environ 2>/dev/null; grep -ls MYSQL_PWD /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/environment /etc/profile.d/* /root/.bashrc /root/.bash_profile /root/.profile /home/*/.bashrc /home/*/.bash_profile /home/*/.profile 2>/dev/null; } | wc -l); echo $c

remediation.command: Remove MYSQL_PWD from /etc/profile, /etc/bashrc and user profiles, unset it in running service environments, use ~/.my.cnf (mode 600) or mysql_config_editor login paths, and delete temporary key scripts left from installation.

title: Ensure Passwords Are Not Passed via the Command Line
description: When using the MySQL client or TDSQL tools, passwords should not be specified via the command-line arguments -p<password> or --password=. Counts running MySQL client processes and shell-history entries that pass a password inline (-p<password> or --password=). Restricted to MySQL client tools to avoid false matches such as mkdir -p.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure Passwords Are Not Passed via the Command Line

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v tdsql_cli_pw_audit | grep -cE '(mysql|mysqladmin|mysqldump|mysqlbinlog|mysqlsh)[^|;]*[[:space:]](-p[^[:space:]]|--password=)' || true); h=$(cat /root/.bash_history /home/*/.bash_history 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '(mysql|mysqladmin|mysqldump|mysqlbinlog|mysqlsh)[^|;]*[[:space:]](-p[^[:space:]]|--password=)' || true); echo $((p + h)) # tdsql_cli_pw_audit

remediation.command: Use a MySQL option file (~/.my.cnf with [client] user/password, mode 600) or the TDSQL encrypted credential system instead of -p<password>; clear affected shell history entries and rotate any exposed passwords.

title: Ensure Operating System Patches Are Up to Date
description: The operating system hosting TDSQL should have the latest security patches installed. Counts pending security updates (dnf/yum updateinfo list security, or apt list --upgradable entries from security pockets). Uses the locally cached repository metadata; refresh it (yum makecache / apt update) before scanning.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Ensure Operating System Patches Are Up to Date

audit.command: if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then pm=$(command -v dnf || command -v yum); out=$($pm -q updateinfo list security 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '[^[:space:]]' || true; elif command -v apt >/dev/null 2>&1; then out=$(apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -ci security || true; else exit 1; fi

remediation.command: Apply security updates during a maintenance window: yum update --security (RHEL/CentOS) or apt update && apt upgrade (Debian/Ubuntu), restarting TDSQL components one node at a time.

title: Ensure TDSQL Is Installed from a Trusted Source
description: TDSQL binaries should be obtained only from trusted, verified sources. Package integrity should be verified via checksums or digital signatures before deployment.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure TDSQL Is Installed from a Trusted Source

audit.command: # Verify binary integrity sha256sum /path/to/tdsql/bin/oss_server sha256sum /path/to/tdsql/bin/scheduler # Compare against the published checksums

remediation.command: Download TDSQL only from official repositories. When building from source: cd /path/to/TDSQL_OSS/build ./build.sh -j Maintain a checksum record of deployed binaries.

title: Ensure a Backup and Recovery Strategy Is Configured
description: TDSQL should be configured with a complete backup strategy. Supported methods include: Physical backup (XtraBackup): enabled by default (xtrabackup="1") Logical backup (mydumper): optional (mydumper="0") ZooKeeper data backup: metadata backed up to local files (/data/home/zkback/) Storage backends: local filesystem (/tdsqlbackup/), COS, OBS, S3, HDFS, DBS.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Ensure a Backup and Recovery Strategy Is Configured

audit.command: # Check the backup configuration in scheduler.xml grep -A5 '<backup' /path/to/tdsql/conf/scheduler.xml # Expected: xtrabackup="1" # Check the ZK backup configuration cat /path/to/tdsql/conf/backupConf.xml # Verify the backup directory ls -la /tdsqlbackup/ 2>/dev/null

remediation.command: Enable physical backup with incremental support in scheduler.xml: <backup increment_flag="1" increment_interval_day="1" mydumper="0" xtrabackup="1" /> Configure the ZK backup retention policy in backupConf.xml: <backup backupfile_save_dir="/data/home/zkback" resv_capacity="800" resv_days="30"> Configure off-site backups (COS/S3/HDFS) for disaster recovery. Test recovery regularly.

title: Ensure Backup Data Is Encrypted
description: Backup data should be encrypted at rest for all backup types: physical backup (XtraBackup), logical backup (mydumper), and ZooKeeper data backup.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure Backup Data Is Encrypted

audit.command: Confirm backups are encrypted: the xtrabackup/mydumper command lines carry --aesencrypt (ps -ef | grep -E "xtrabackup|mydumper" | grep -- --aesencrypt) and OSS backup metadata shows aesencrypt=1; local backup volumes use LUKS (lsblk -f | grep -i crypt); COS/S3 targets enforce server-side encryption. Unencrypted backups are a finding.

remediation.command: TDSQL provides AES + cluster-key based backup encryption at the backup layer (-- aesencrypt and --cluster_identify command-line arguments). To enable it: 1. Modify the cluster backup policy in the OSS management platform to enable backup encryption: <!-- scheduler.xml backup section --> <backup increment_flag="1" increment_interval_day="1" mydumper="0" xtrabackup="1" aesencrypt="1" /> 2.

title: Ensure Sensitive Configuration Data Is Encrypted
description: Sensitive data in configuration files (passwords, keys, connection strings) should be stored in encrypted form. TDSQL provides AES encryption and base64 encoding for credential protection.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7 Ensure Sensitive Configuration Data Is Encrypted

audit.command: # Check for cleartext passwords in the configuration grep -rn 'password' /path/to/tdsql/conf/ | grep -v '#' | head -20 # Encrypted passwords appear as long base64-encoded strings. # Short, simple cleartext strings indicate unencrypted passwords.

remediation.command: Encrypt all passwords using TDSQL's encryption tools. Ensure the master key used for encryption is stored separately from the encrypted data and managed by an independent key management process. Integrating with a KMS is strongly recommended. Encryption process overview: 1.

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on TDSQL Data Directories
description: TDSQL data directories and MySQL instance data directories should have restrictive permissions. Only the TDSQL service account should have read/write access. TDSQL creates data directories with 0755 by default, but stricter permissions are recommended. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_DATA (default /data/tdsql/data) for the instance data directory. Counts files that grant the listed permission to other users; any match fails, and a missing directory fails. (o+rw; sockets and symlinks excluded). Expected: directories 0750, files 0640, owner tdsql/mysql.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure Correct Permissions on TDSQL Data Directories

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" ! -type l ! -type s -perm /o+rw -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 750 <data dir>; find <data dir> -type d -exec chmod 750 {} +; find <data dir> -type f -exec chmod 640 {} +; chown -R tdsql:tdsql <data dir> (or mysql:mysql for instance files).

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on TDSQL Configuration Files
description: TDSQL configuration files contain sensitive information (encrypted passwords, ZK connection strings, encryption keys, network topology). Key files include: scheduler.xml - main configuration file oss.json - OSS runtime configuration manager.json - Manager runtime configuration mysql.xml - MySQL variable whitelist proxy.json - Proxy configuration backupConf.xml - backup configuration plugin.json - plugin configuration The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql). Counts files that grant the listed permission to other users; any match fails, and a missing directory fails. (o+r). Expected: files 0640, directories 0750.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure Correct Permissions on TDSQL Configuration Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/conf"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/conf"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" ! -type l -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 750 <tdsql>/conf; chown -R tdsql:tdsql <tdsql>/conf; chmod 640 <tdsql>/conf/*.xml <tdsql>/conf/*.json

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on SSL/TLS Certificate Files
description: SSL/TLS certificate and key files must have appropriately restrictive permissions. TDSQL certificate files include: OSS service: ../boot/ca.key, ../boot/ca.crt PEM files: ca-cert.pem, ca-key.pem, server-req.pem SQLEngine instances: <module_dir>/<port>/sqlengine/etc/{ca- cert,server-cert,server-key}.pem Gateway: <module_dir>/<port>/gateway/conf/{ca-cert,server- cert,server-key}.pem Private key files require strict ... The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql) and TDSQL_DATA. Counts private keys (*.key, *key*.pem) with any group/other permission and certificates writable by group/other; expected keys 0400/0600 and certificates 0644 or stricter.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure Correct Permissions on SSL/TLS Certificate Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/boot" "${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}"; do [ -d "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/boot" "${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}"; do [ -d "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" -type f \( -name '*.key' -o -name '*key*.pem' \) -perm /077 -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l) + $(find "$p" -type f \( -name '*.crt' -o -name '*.pem' \) -perm /022 -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 600 <tdsql>/boot/ca.key <tdsql>/boot/ca-key.pem and instance *key*.pem files; chmod 644 certificates; chown tdsql:tdsql (or mysql:mysql for instance certificates).

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on the TDSQL Binary Directory
description: The binary directory (bin/) contains the executables for all TDSQL components: oss_server, scheduler, startup/shutdown scripts, and Python integration scripts. These files must be protected against unauthorized modification. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql). Counts files that grant the listed permission to other users; any match fails, and a missing directory fails. (o+w). Expected: directory 0750, binaries owned by root:tdsql.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.5 Ensure Correct Permissions on the TDSQL Binary Directory

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/bin"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/bin"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" ! -type l -perm /o+w -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 750 <tdsql>/bin <tdsql>/bin/*; chown root:tdsql <tdsql>/bin <tdsql>/bin/*

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on the TDSQL Boot Directory
description: The boot directory (boot/) contains Python modules, SSL certificates, and initialization scripts. Because it includes SSL private keys and operations modules, it must be properly protected. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql). Counts files that grant the listed permission to other users; any match fails, and a missing directory fails. (o+rw). Expected: directory 0750, CA keys 0600.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.6 Ensure Correct Permissions on the TDSQL Boot Directory

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/boot"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/boot"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" ! -type l -perm /o+rw -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 750 <tdsql>/boot; chown -R tdsql:tdsql <tdsql>/boot; chmod 600 <tdsql>/boot/ca.key <tdsql>/boot/ca-key.pem

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on Backup Directories
description: TDSQL backup directories must have restrictive permissions. Backup files contain complete copies of the database. Key paths: Local backup: /tdsqlbackup/ (default) ZooKeeper backup: /data/home/zkback/ Checks /tdsqlbackup and /data/home/zkback (at least one must exist). Counts files that grant the listed permission to other users; any match fails, and a missing directory fails. (o+r). Expected: directories 0750.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.7 Ensure Correct Permissions on Backup Directories

audit.command: n=0; for p in "/tdsqlbackup" "/data/home/zkback"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "/tdsqlbackup" "/data/home/zkback"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" ! -type l -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 750 /tdsqlbackup /data/home/zkback; chown tdsql:tdsql /tdsqlbackup /data/home/zkback; find /tdsqlbackup -type f -exec chmod 640 {} +

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Tablespace Files
description: MySQL InnoDB tablespace files (.ibd), the system tablespace (ibdata*), redo log files (ib_logfile*), and undo tablespace files should have restrictive permissions. Uses TDSQL_DATA (default /data/tdsql/data) for the instance data directory. Counts *.ibd, ibdata* and ib_logfile* files readable by other users; expected 0640, owner mysql:mysql.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.8 Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Tablespace Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" -type f \( -name '*.ibd' -o -name 'ibdata*' -o -name 'ib_logfile*' \) -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: find <data dir> \( -name '*.ibd' -o -name 'ibdata*' -o -name 'ib_logfile*' \) -exec chmod 640 {} + and chown mysql:mysql them.

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Binary Log Files
description: Binary log files (binlog.*, mysql-bin.*) contain records of all data modifications and must have restrictive permissions. Searches /data/tdsql (the benchmark path). Counts binlog.*, mysql-bin.* and relay-log.* files readable by other users; expected 0640.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.9 Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Binary Log Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" -type f \( -name 'binlog.*' -o -name 'mysql-bin.*' -o -name 'relay-log.*' \) -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: find /data/tdsql \( -name 'binlog.*' -o -name 'mysql-bin.*' -o -name 'relay-log.*' \) -exec chmod 640 {} +

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on Audit Log Files
description: If MySQL audit logging is enabled, the audit log files must have restrictive permissions. Audit logs are critical for security monitoring and forensic analysis. Searches /data/tdsql (the benchmark path; confirm audit_txsql_audit_dir points inside it). Counts audit files accessible by other users; expected 0600 or 0640, owner mysql:mysql.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.12 Ensure Correct Permissions on Audit Log Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" -type f -name '*audit*' -perm /o+rw -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: find /data/tdsql -name '*audit*' -type f -exec chmod 640 {} +; chown mysql:mysql those files.

title: Ensure `local_infile` Is Disabled
description: The local_infile parameter controls whether clients are allowed to use the LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE statement. Enabling this feature can be abused by an attacker to read arbitrary files on the client host through carefully crafted SQL statements. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure `local_infile` Is Disabled

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.local_infile" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set the instance parameter local_infile = OFF through the TDSQL management platform (OSS) or SET GLOBAL local_infile = OFF; and persist it in the parameter template.

title: Ensure No Anonymous Accounts Exist
description: Anonymous accounts (with an empty username '') allow any user to log in to the database without specifying a username. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure No Anonymous Accounts Exist

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE User = ''" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: DROP USER ''@'localhost'; DROP USER ''@'%'; (for every anonymous account returned).

title: Ensure the `root` Account Is Disabled or Hardened
description: MySQL's root superuser account holds all privileges. In the TDSQL architecture, instance management is performed by system accounts (tdsqlsys_*), and root should not be used for daily operations.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure the `root` Account Is Disabled or Hardened

audit.command: 1. Check whether TDSQL has forbidden root user operations: # Check whether root is forbidden in the OSS configuration grep "forbidden" <oss_config> | grep "root" 2. Check the root account status in the MySQL instance: SELECT User, Host, account_locked FROM mysql.user WHERE User = 'root';

remediation.command: 1. Ensure the OSS configuration db_user_root.forbidden = true (the TDSQL default). 2. If a root account exists, lock it: ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' ACCOUNT LOCK; 3. Or change the root password to a strong random value and store it only in a secure password management system.

title: Ensure No High-Privilege Accounts Use Wildcard Hostnames
description: A MySQL Host field of % allows connections from any IP. High-privilege accounts (especially those holding SUPER, FILE, SHUTDOWN, etc.) should not use wildcard hostnames. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure No High-Privilege Accounts Use Wildcard Hostnames

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE Host = '%' AND (Super_priv = 'Y' OR File_priv = 'Y' OR Shutdown_priv = 'Y' OR Grant_priv = 'Y') AND User NOT LIKE 'tdsqlsys%'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: RENAME USER '<user>'@'%' TO '<user>'@'<approved subnet, e.g. 10.0.0.%>'; for every high-privilege account returned.

title: Ensure No Excessive `SUPER` Privilege Grants
description: The SUPER privilege allows many dangerous operations, including modifying global variables, killing other users' queries, and bypassing read-only restrictions.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5 Ensure No Excessive `SUPER` Privilege Grants

audit.command: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE Super_priv = 'Y'; Confirm only TDSQL system accounts (such as the necessary tdsqlsys_kp_new) hold the SUPER privilege.

remediation.command: Revoke the SUPER privilege from unnecessary users: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM 'username'@'host'; In MySQL 8.0, use fine-grained dynamic privileges (such as SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN, CONNECTION_ADMIN) instead of SUPER.

title: Ensure No Excessive `FILE` Privilege Grants
description: The FILE privilege allows users to read and write server filesystem files via LOAD DATA INFILE, SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE, LOAD_FILE(), and similar.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.6 Ensure No Excessive `FILE` Privilege Grants

audit.command: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE File_priv = 'Y'; Confirm only accounts that genuinely require it hold this privilege.

remediation.command: REVOKE FILE ON *.* FROM 'username'@'host';

title: Ensure TXSQL System User Hiding and Anti-Forgery Is Enabled
description: The TXSQL kernel provides three layers of protection for system user reserved prefixes (tdsqlsys, tdsql3_sys, controlled by the tdsql_system_user_prefix variable): 1. Hidden visibility - the mysql.user view automatically masks system user rows. 2. Forgery prevention - no client is allowed to create users with the system user reserved prefixes. 3.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.11 Ensure TXSQL System User Hiding and Anti-Forgery Is Enabled

audit.command: -- 1. Execute after logging in as a regular user (should not see tdsqlsys_* users) SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE User LIKE 'tdsqlsys_%'; -- 2. Attempt to create a user with the same prefix (should be rejected by the kernel) CREATE USER 'tdsqlsys_attacker'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'fake_pass'; -- ERROR XXXX: User 'tdsqlsys_attacker' is reserved for system use. -- 3. Attempt to write directly via INSERT (should be rejected by the kernel) INSERT INTO mysql.user (User, Host) VALUES ('tdsqlsys_evil','%'); -- ERROR XXXX: Modifying system tables is not allowed. -- 4.

remediation.command: These protections are enabled by default out of the box in TDSQL. If system users are visible or can be created, the cluster is not running the TXSQL kernel or has been replaced with stock MySQL, and must be upgraded to the TXSQL kernel.

title: Ensure the Callable Scope of OSS Sensitive Interfaces Is Restricted
description: OSS provides two layers of interface-level access control: interface_mask (sensitive interface allowlist) and deny_interfacename (interface denylist): interface_mask (oss.json:240-246) - lists interfaces that only authenticated privileged callers may invoke (such as TDSQL.AddUser, TDSQL.ResetPwd, TDSQL.GetKmsConfig, TDSQL.CreateKmsConfig).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.12 Ensure the Callable Scope of OSS Sensitive Interfaces Is Restricted

audit.command: Run grep -A2 interface_mask <tdsql>/conf/oss.json and grep "<deny_interfacename" <tdsql>/conf/scheduler.xml. The mask must include TDSQL.AddUser, AddMultiUser, ModifyOssUser, ResetPwd, RegisterOssUser, ListUser, GetKmsConfig, CreateKmsConfig, ReplaceIp, ForceSwitchInstance, ForceSwitchMaster and ForceDelInstance; any missing interface is a finding.

remediation.command: Extend the sensitive interface list in oss.json: { "name": "interface_mask", "value": "TDSQL.AddUser,TDSQL.ListUser,TDSQL.AddMultiUser,TDSQL.RegisterOssUser,TDSQL.Modif yOssUser,TDSQL.ResetPwd,TDSQL.GetKmsConfig,TDSQL.CreateKmsConfig,TDSQL.ReplaceIp,T DSQL.ForceSwitchInstance,TDSQL.DeleteInstance" } Add denylist interfaces in scheduler.xml (callable by no one): <deny_interfacename name="TDSQL.ReplaceIp"/> <deny_interfacename ...

title: Ensure TXSQL Auditing Is Enabled on All Data Nodes
description: TDSQL provides the audit_txsql audit facility to record SQL activity on TXSQL data nodes. Auditing must be enabled consistently on every primary and replica in every shard so that a node switch or distributed query cannot create an audit blind spot. ALL mode records all SQL activity. FILTER mode uses database, source-IP, and user exclusion lists and therefore requires a formally approved exception. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Run against every primary and replica of every shard. Passes when the audit_txsql plugin is ACTIVE, audit_txsql_audit_mode = ALL and the db/ip/user filters are empty; also confirm audit files are written in audit_txsql_audit_dir with complete records.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure TXSQL Auditing Is Enabled on All Data Nodes

audit.command: pl=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_NAME = 'audit_txsql' AND PLUGIN_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('audit_txsql_audit_mode', 'audit_txsql_filter_db', 'audit_txsql_filter_ip', 'audit_txsql_filter_user')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "audit_txsql_audit_mode" {m = toupper($2)} $1 ~ /^audit_txsql_filter_/ && $2 != "" {f++} END {print (m == "ALL" && f == 0) ? "ok" : "bad"}'); [ "$pl" -ge 1 ] && [ "$r" = ok ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL audit_txsql_audit_mode = 'ALL'; (with empty audit_txsql_filter_db/ip/user) through a TDSQL custom parameter template associated with every instance.

title: Ensure the TDSQL Password Complexity Policy Is Enabled
description: Password complexity for database accounts must be enforced through the supported TDSQL management-platform account policy. The policy should define an organization- approved minimum length and required character classes.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2 Ensure the TDSQL Password Complexity Policy Is Enabled

audit.command: 1. Review the password policy configured in the TDSQL management platform for the target 8.0 instances. 2. Confirm that minimum length and character-class requirements meet the organization standard. 3. Confirm that accounts are created and modified through the TDSQL management platform. 4. Review a recent approved password-change record to confirm enforcement.

remediation.command: Configure the required password strength in the TDSQL management platform and use the platform to rotate non-compliant credentials. Do not install or rely on the upstream validate_password component unless Tencent confirms support for the exact TXSQL version and deployment mode.

title: Ensure Credentials Are Stored Encrypted
description: Database passwords, API keys, and other credentials in TDSQL component configuration files should be stored encrypted and must not appear in cleartext.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.5 Ensure Credentials Are Stored Encrypted

audit.command: Inspect scheduler.xml (oc_tool password, audit_database password, super_user pwd, manager_db password, whitelist user_password tokens) and oss.json system-account *_pwd_encrypt fields. Every password/token must be in encrypted form (long base64/ciphertext); any short readable or cleartext value is a finding.

remediation.command: 1. TDSQL provides an AES encryption tool that encrypts all passwords with the cluster master key: Passwords are stored in encrypted form in ZooKeeper. Password fields in configuration files should be filled in after processing with the encryption tool. 2. The cluster master key should be generated independently for each cluster via the deployment-side key injection process and provided at runtime via an environment variable or KMS;

title: Ensure KMS Is Deployed and Instance Data Encryption Is Enabled
description: TDSQL TDE depends on an available KMS, a valid cluster-level KMS configuration, and the instance-level Data Encryption switch being enabled in the management platform.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.1 Ensure KMS Is Deployed and Instance Data Encryption Is Enabled

audit.command: 1. Confirm that all configured KMS nodes are healthy. 2. In Cluster Management -> KMS Configuration, verify the approved endpoint, protocol, service domain, and credentials. 3. In Instance Management -> Instance Details -> Basic Information, confirm Data Encryption is enabled for each in-scope instance. 4. Confirm the KMS keyring configuration is present: SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'keyring_kms_file'; 5. Create and verify a controlled encrypted test table.

remediation.command: 1. Deploy KMS with the TDSQL one-click package and supported playbooks/tdsql_kms.yml procedure. 2. Create a dedicated KMS business account and obtain its SecretId and SecretKey. 3. Add the KMS endpoint and credentials in Cluster Management -> KMS Configuration; use an HA VIP in production. 4. Enable Data Encryption in the target instance's basic information. 5. Validate encrypted-table creation as described in 8.2.

title: Ensure InnoDB Tablespace Encryption Is Enabled for Sensitive Tables
description: TDSQL supports per-table InnoDB transparent encryption through ENCRYPTION='Y'. Every table in the organization's approved sensitive-data inventory must be encrypted. The default algorithm for international deployments is AES.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.2 Ensure InnoDB Tablespace Encryption Is Enabled for Sensitive Tables

audit.command: 1. Obtain the approved inventory of schemas and tables containing sensitive data. 2. Query those tablespaces: SELECT NAME, ENCRYPTION, ENCRYPTION_ALGORITHM FROM information_schema.INNODB_TABLESPACES WHERE NAME IN ('schema1/table1', 'schema2/table2'); SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'innodb_encryption_algorithm'; Confirm every in-scope table has ENCRYPTION = 'Y' and algorithm AES.

remediation.command: Ensure 8.1 is satisfied, then create or alter each sensitive table through the approved change process: CREATE TABLE schema_name.sensitive_table (...) ENCRYPTION='Y'; ALTER TABLE schema_name.existing_sensitive_table ENCRYPTION='Y'; Set innodb_encryption_algorithm to AES through Instance Management -> Parameter Configuration -> Parameter Settings when required.

title: Ensure SSL/TLS Is Enabled on MySQL Instances
description: MySQL instances should enable SSL/TLS to encrypt communication between clients and the database. Unencrypted connections can be sniffed on the network, leading to credential and data leakage. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Passes when have_ssl = YES; where enforcement is required also confirm require_secure_transport = ON.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.1 Ensure SSL/TLS Is Enabled on MySQL Instances

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.have_ssl" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Deploy the SSL certificate files (3.4), configure ssl-ca / ssl-cert / ssl-key in [mysqld] (or enable SSL centrally through OSS) and set require_secure_transport = ON where encryption must be enforced.

title: Ensure SQLEngine-to-Data-Node Communication Is Encrypted
description: Communication between the TDSQL SQLEngine (proxy layer) and backend data nodes should be encrypted with SSL. Passes when tdsql_conn_datanode_ssl_mode and tdsql_conn_system_ssl_mode are at least REQUIRED (VERIFY_CA recommended). Runs the mysql client against the SQLEngine (compute node) selected by TDSQL_SQLENGINE_OPTS (falls back to TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.2 Ensure SQLEngine-to-Data-Node Communication Is Encrypted

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_SQLENGINE_OPTS:-${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-}} -NBe "SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'tdsql_conn_datanode_ssl_mode'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; a=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "tdsql_conn_datanode_ssl_mode" {print toupper($2)}'); out2=$(mysql ${TDSQL_SQLENGINE_OPTS:-${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-}} -NBe "SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'tdsql_conn_system_ssl_mode'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(printf '%s\n' "$out2" | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "tdsql_conn_system_ssl_mode" {print toupper($2)}'); case "$a" in REQUIRED|VERIFY_CA|VERIFY_IDENTITY) ;; *) echo "datanode $a"; exit 0;; esac; case "$b" in REQUIRED|VERIFY_CA|VERIFY_IDENTITY) echo compliant;; *) echo "system $b";; esac

remediation.command: Enable three-tier SSL through the OSS SSL centralized-enablement interface: tdsql_enable_ssl = ON, tdsql_conn_datanode_ssl_mode = VERIFY_CA and tdsql_conn_system_ssl_mode = REQUIRED (or stricter).

title: Ensure the Gateway Has SSL Enabled
description: The TDSQL Gateway is the entry point for client connections and should enable SSL to protect communication between clients and the gateway. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.3 Ensure the Gateway Has SSL Enabled

audit.command: In the OSS management platform (or the Gateway proxy.json) check gateway.mode.ssl.open for every instance: 0 (the default, disabled) is a finding; 1 enables optional encryption, 2 enforces encryption (recommended) and 3 adds mutual authentication.

remediation.command: Modify the Gateway parameter via the OSS management platform: { "Name": "gateway.mode.ssl.open", "value": "2" }

title: Ensure SSL Is Enabled on the Replication Link
description: The data stream of MySQL primary-replica replication should be encrypted with SSL to prevent replication data from being eavesdropped on the network. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Run on replicas: passes when every replication channel shows Master_SSL_Allowed: Yes. A node that is not a replica (empty SHOW REPLICA STATUS) passes because it has no inbound replication link.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 10.1 Ensure SSL Is Enabled on the Replication Link

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -e 'SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G' 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ -z "$out" ]; then echo compliant; else n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'Master_SSL_Allowed: Yes' || true); t=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'Master_SSL_Allowed:' || true); [ "$t" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" -eq "$t" ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Configure replication SSL through the TDSQL management platform (inter-component SSL, 9.2), or STOP REPLICA; CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_SSL = 1, SOURCE_SSL_CA = ...; START REPLICA;

title: Ensure the Replication User Has Minimal Privileges
description: The replication-dedicated account (tdsqlsys_repl) should hold only the minimum privileges necessary for replication. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Counts grant lines for 'tdsqlsys_repl'@'%' that contain anything other than REPLICATION SLAVE / REPLICATION CLIENT (or USAGE) on *.*.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 10.2 Ensure the Replication User Has Minimal Privileges

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SHOW GRANTS FOR 'tdsqlsys_repl'@'%'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -vcE '^GRANT (USAGE|REPLICATION SLAVE|REPLICATION CLIENT)(, (REPLICATION SLAVE|REPLICATION CLIENT))* ON \*\.\* TO ' || true

remediation.command: REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* FROM 'tdsqlsys_repl'@'%'; GRANT REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.* TO 'tdsqlsys_repl'@'%'; (coordinate with the TDSQL Manager, which manages this account).

title: Ensure ZooKeeper ACLs Are Enabled
description: TDSQL uses ZooKeeper to store cluster metadata, configuration information, and to coordinate node state. ZooKeeper ACLs (Access Control Lists) control access to ZNodes. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql); reads <TDSQL_HOME>/conf/scheduler.xml and passes when <zookeeper> has safeacl="1". Also confirm with zkCli.sh getAcl /tdsql that the ACL is not world:anyone:cdrwa.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 11.1 Ensure ZooKeeper ACLs Are Enabled

audit.command: f="${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/conf/scheduler.xml"; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1; if grep -Eo '<zookeeper[^>]*' "$f" | grep -Eq '[[:space:]]safeacl="1"'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Set safeacl="1" on the <zookeeper> element of scheduler.xml, configure digest ACLs with a strong random credential and restart the affected components.

title: Ensure OC Tool Credentials Are Changed and Use a Least-Privilege Account
description: OC Tool is the TDSQL operations control tool used to perform management operations on target machines (such as installing components and launching instances). Its username should be a dedicated least-privilege account rather than root, and its password should be a strong random value stored encrypted.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 12.1 Ensure OC Tool Credentials Are Changed and Use a Least-Privilege Account

audit.command: Check the OC Tool configuration in scheduler.xml: <oc_tool ... user="..." password="..." .../> Confirm: 1. user is not root, but a dedicated least-privilege account (such as tdsql_oc). 2. The password field is encrypted (a long base64/ciphertext string) and differs from the install template's initial value. diff <(grep oc_tool /path/to/installed/conf/scheduler.xml) \ <(grep oc_tool /path/to/install_template/scheduler.xml)

remediation.command: 1. Create a dedicated least-privilege operations account (non-root) on all TDSQL nodes. 2. Configure sudoers to grant only the necessary privileged commands. 3. Set a strong random password and store it encrypted. 4. Update the scheduler.xml configuration: <oc_tool ... user="tdsql_oc" password="<encrypted_strong_password>" .../>

title: Ensure Manager Database Credentials Are Encrypted
description: The credential (tdsqlsys_kp_new) used by the TDSQL Manager to connect to MySQL instances should be stored encrypted.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 12.2 Ensure Manager Database Credentials Are Encrypted

audit.command: Check the Manager DB configuration in scheduler.xml: <manager_db user="tdsqlsys_kp_new" password="..." /> Confirm the password field is encrypted (base64-encoded, length >= 24 bytes), not a short readable string. Also verify the value differs from the install template's initial value.

remediation.command: Encrypt the password using the TDSQL encryption tool: # Encrypt with the cluster master key (see section 2.6 for tool details) /path/to/tdsql/bin/crypt_tool -e "<cluster_master_key>" "<plain_password>" # Put the resulting ciphertext into the manager_db.password field of scheduler.xml

title: Ensure Access to KMS Configuration Interfaces Is Restricted
description: The KMS configuration interfaces (TDSQL.GetKmsConfig, TDSQL.CreateKmsConfig) involve master key (CMK) management; abuse can defeat the entire cluster's encryption. OSS should: Include the KMS interfaces in interface_mask so only privileged users can invoke them. Mask the keyring_kms_config field in return values in the audit log (see property_mask in oss.json:230-237).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 12.9 Ensure Access to KMS Configuration Interfaces Is Restricted

audit.command: # 1. Confirm the KMS interfaces are included in the mask grep 'TDSQL.GetKmsConfig\|TDSQL.CreateKmsConfig' /path/to/tdsql/conf/oss.json # 2. Confirm the KMS configuration field is included in response masking grep 'keyring_kms_config' /path/to/tdsql/conf/oss.json # 3. Verify KMS service health (via the OSS KMS status query interface)

remediation.command: { "name": "interface_mask", "value": "...,TDSQL.GetKmsConfig,TDSQL.CreateKmsConfig" }, { "name": "property_mask", "value": "pwd,password,secretid,secretkey,token,secret_id,secret_key,ca_cert,server_cert,se rver_key,client_cert,client_key,keyring_kms_config" }

title: Ensure OSS Interface Signature Authentication Is Hardened
description: TDSQL OSS uses caller + password interface signature authentication (scheduler.xml line 25: <whitelist user_password="DES,...;@osssuper,..."/>). Each caller uses an independent pre-shared credential pair, avoiding lateral movement caused by credential reuse.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 12.10 Ensure OSS Interface Signature Authentication Is Hardened

audit.command: # 1. Check the allowlist format (should be "caller1,encrypted_password1;caller2,encrypted_password2") grep '<whitelist' /path/to/tdsql/conf/scheduler.xml # 2. Confirm each upstream system uses an independent caller # e.g., the CAM gateway uses caller=cam_gw, monitoring uses caller=monitor_svc # 3. Verify caller credentials are encrypted (no cleartext should appear)

remediation.command: <whitelist ip="10.0.1.0/24;10.0.2.100" user_password="cam_gw,<encrypted_token>;monitor_svc,<encrypted_token>;@osssuper, <encrypted_token>" /> For each upstream system: Must have an independent caller. The password is encrypted via crypt_tool -e or tdsql_encrypt -e (see section 2.6). An IP allowlist restricts source addresses. Credentials are rotated periodically (consistent with the 11.8 OSS super user rotation policy).

title: Ensure the TDSQL Database Is Placed on a Non-System Partition
description: TDSQL database instance data (including MySQL data files, binary logs, and transaction logs) should be stored on a dedicated, non-system partition. In TDSQL, the data directory and log directory paths can be configured per host via the ZooKeeper set_hostdir node. Uses TDSQL_DATA (default /data/tdsql/data) for the instance data directory; passes when it is not on the /, /var or /usr filesystem.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure the TDSQL Database Is Placed on a Non-System Partition

audit.command: d=${TDSQL_DATA:-/data/tdsql/data}; [ -d "$d" ] || exit 1; m=$(findmnt -n -o TARGET -T "$d" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$m" in /|/var|/usr) echo "on $m";; *) echo compliant;; esac

remediation.command: Create a dedicated partition/volume for TDSQL data (e.g. mounted at /data/tdsql with nodev), migrate the data directory to it during a maintenance window and add it to /etc/fstab.

title: Ensure Interactive Login Is Disabled for TDSQL Service Accounts
description: The operating system accounts running TDSQL services should have interactive login disabled (shell set to /sbin/nologin or /bin/false). Passes when the tdsql account (and mysql, if present) has /sbin/nologin or /bin/false as its shell; FAILs when no tdsql account exists.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure Interactive Login Is Disabled for TDSQL Service Accounts

audit.command: u=$(getent passwd tdsql) || exit 1; bad=0; for a in tdsql mysql; do s=$(getent passwd "$a" | cut -d: -f7) || continue; case "$s" in /sbin/nologin|/usr/sbin/nologin|/bin/false|/usr/bin/false) ;; *) bad=1;; esac; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo 'interactive shell'

remediation.command: usermod -s /sbin/nologin tdsql; usermod -s /sbin/nologin mysql

title: Ensure Appropriate System Resource Limits Are Configured
description: Operating system resource limits (ulimits) should be properly configured for TDSQL processes, particularly the number of open file descriptors, maximum processes, and memory locking. Passes when /etc/security/limits.conf or limits.d sets hard nofile and nproc limits of at least 65535 for the tdsql user (the benchmark baseline). For systemd-managed components also confirm LimitNOFILE/LimitNPROC in the unit.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.9 Ensure Appropriate System Resource Limits Are Configured

audit.command: out=$(cat /etc/security/limits.conf /etc/security/limits.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1 == "tdsql" && $2 == "hard" && $3 == "nofile" && ($4 == "unlimited" || $4 + 0 >= 65535) {f++} $1 == "tdsql" && $2 == "hard" && $3 == "nproc" && ($4 == "unlimited" || $4 + 0 >= 65535) {p++} END {print (f && p) ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}'

remediation.command: Add to /etc/security/limits.conf: tdsql soft nofile 65535; tdsql hard nofile 65535; tdsql soft nproc 65535; tdsql hard nproc 65535; tdsql soft memlock unlimited; tdsql hard memlock unlimited; then restart the components.

title: Ensure Dedicated Hosts Are Used for TDSQL Components
description: TDSQL components should be deployed on dedicated hosts that do not run other application workloads. This applies to all components: OSS, Manager/Scheduler/Keeper, MySQL instances, Proxy, and ZooKeeper.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure Dedicated Hosts Are Used for TDSQL Components

audit.command: # Check for non-TDSQL processes listening on network ports ss -tlnp | grep -v -E '(mysqld|oss_server|scheduler|zookeeper|tdsqlproxy|oc_agent)' # Review running processes ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -20

remediation.command: Deploy TDSQL on dedicated hosts. Remove unnecessary software packages. Use TDSQL's set/group architecture to achieve component isolation.

title: Ensure Backup Recovery Is Tested Regularly
description: The backup recovery process should be tested regularly, including full restore and point- in-time recovery.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5 Ensure Backup Recovery Is Tested Regularly

audit.command: # Review the following documentation: # - Date of the most recent successful recovery test # - Documented recovery procedures # - Measured recovery time # - Data integrity verification results

remediation.command: 1. Establish a quarterly backup recovery test schedule. 2. Document recovery procedures for each backup type. 3. Test in an isolated environment. 4. Record and review recovery results.

title: Ensure TDSQL Component Versions Are Consistent Across the Cluster
description: All TDSQL components in a cluster should run the same version to avoid compatibility issues and ensure security patches are applied uniformly.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.10 Ensure TDSQL Component Versions Are Consistent Across the Cluster

audit.command: On every node run <tdsql>/bin/oss_server --version and <tdsql>/bin/scheduler --version, or call the OSS TDSQL.GetDbVersion / TDSQL.TdsqlModuleVersion interfaces for the cluster, and compare the results. All OSS, Scheduler/Keeper, Agent, Gateway and data-node versions must match across the cluster; a mismatch outside a planned rolling upgrade is a finding.

remediation.command: Plan and execute a rolling upgrade to ensure version consistency. Follow the TDSQL upgrade documentation.

title: Ensure Adequate Disk Space Monitoring Is Configured
description: Disk space monitoring with alerting should be configured for all TDSQL partitions (data, log, backup, temporary directories). TDSQL includes a built-in log cleanup mechanism: OSS logs are retained for up to 30 days / 100 GB (cleaned every 12 hours), and Manager logs up to 20 GB (cleaned every 3 minutes).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.11 Ensure Adequate Disk Space Monitoring Is Configured

audit.command: # Check current disk usage df -h /data/tdsql/ /tdsqlbackup/ /data/home/zkback/ 2>/dev/null # Check the TDSQL log cleanup configuration grep -A3 'log_clean' /path/to/tdsql/conf/scheduler.xml grep -A3 'clear_log' /path/to/tdsql/conf/scheduler.xml

remediation.command: 1. Configure disk alerts at 80% and 90% thresholds. 2. Verify that TDSQL log cleanup is enabled: <log_clean enable="1" max_save_days="30" max_size="100000000000" hz="12"/> <clear_log enable="on" resv_capacity="20" distance_time="3" /> 3. Deploy external monitoring (Prometheus, Zabbix) covering all TDSQL partitions.

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on TDSQL Log Directories
description: TDSQL log directories should have restrictive permissions. Log files may contain sensitive information. TDSQL uses several log directories: OSS logs: ../log/sys_tdsql_oss_log Manager logs: ../log/sys_manager Manager statistics: ../log/stat_manager Backup logs: ../log/sys_backup The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql). Counts files that grant the listed permission to other users; any match fails, and a missing directory fails. (o+r). Expected: directories 0750, files 0640.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure Correct Permissions on TDSQL Log Directories

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/log"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}/log"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" ! -type l -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: chmod 750 <tdsql>/log; chown -R tdsql:tdsql <tdsql>/log; find <tdsql>/log -type f -exec chmod 640 {} +; find <tdsql>/log -type d -exec chmod 750 {} +

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Slow Query Log Files
description: The slow query log records queries exceeding the execution-time threshold and may contain sensitive SQL statements and parameter values. Searches /data/tdsql (the benchmark path; confirm slow_query_log_file points inside it). Counts slow-query log files readable by other users; expected 0640.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.10 Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Slow Query Log Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" -type f -name '*slow*' -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: find /data/tdsql -name '*slow*' -type f -exec chmod 640 {} +; chown mysql:mysql those files.

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Error Log Files
description: The MySQL error log contains diagnostic information including startup/shutdown, errors, warnings, and notes, which may expose sensitive configuration and operational details. Searches /data/tdsql (the benchmark path). Counts *error*.log files readable by other users; expected 0640.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.11 Ensure Correct Permissions on MySQL Error Log Files

audit.command: n=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "/data/tdsql"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" -type f -name '*error*' -name '*.log' -perm /o+r -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: find /data/tdsql -name '*error*' -name '*.log' -exec chmod 640 {} +; chown mysql:mysql those files.

title: Ensure Build and Deployment Artifacts Are Removed from Production
description: Build artifacts and development-time files should not exist on production servers: Build directory (build/) and its temporary build scripts Source code directory (src/) Version control directory (.git) Test scripts and test data The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses TDSQL_HOME (install directory with bin/, conf/, boot/, log/; default /data/tdsql). Counts build directories, .git directories, setenv.sh, C/C++ sources and CMakeLists.txt under the installation; production should have none.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.13 Ensure Build and Deployment Artifacts Are Removed from Production

audit.command: n=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}"; do [ -e "$p" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; [ $n -gt 0 ] || exit 1; c=0; for p in "${TDSQL_HOME:-/data/tdsql}"; do [ -e "$p" ] || continue; c=$((c + $(find "$p" \( -type d \( -name build -o -name .git \) -o -name setenv.sh -o -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.h' -o -name CMakeLists.txt \) -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l))); done; echo $c

remediation.command: Remove build and source artifacts from production nodes (e.g. <tdsql>/build, <tdsql>/src, <tdsql>/.git, CMakeLists.txt, Makefile) after taking a backup and confirming they are not used at runtime.

title: Ensure Correct Permissions on the Temporary File Directory
description: The MySQL tmpdir may contain temporary tables, intermediate query results, and sort files. Its effective location must be placed on a controlled filesystem and be accessible only to the operating-system account that runs the database. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Reads the effective tmpdir from the instance and requires each directory to be owned by a non-root (service) account and not writable by group or other (0700, or 0750 with an approved group). Run on the data-node host; also confirm with findmnt -T that it is on an approved filesystem.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.14 Ensure Correct Permissions on the Temporary File Directory

audit.command: t=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.tmpdir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; bad=0; seen=0; IFS=':'; for d in $t; do seen=1; s=$(stat -Lc '%a %U' "$d" 2>/dev/null) || { bad=1; continue; }; p=${s% *}; o=${s#* }; [ $((0$p & 022)) -eq 0 ] || bad=1; [ "$o" != root ] || bad=1; done; [ $seen -eq 1 ] && [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: install -d -m 0700 -o tdsql -g tdsql /data/tdsql_tmp, set tmpdir to it through the TDSQL custom parameter template and restart the instance.

title: Ensure `secure_file_priv` Is Correctly Configured
description: secure_file_priv restricts the directory for file operations by LOAD DATA INFILE, SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE, and the LOAD_FILE() function. If unset or empty, MySQL can access arbitrary paths on the filesystem. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Passes when secure_file_priv names a specific directory or is NULL (import/export disabled); an empty string fails.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure `secure_file_priv` Is Correctly Configured

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT CASE WHEN @@global.secure_file_priv IS NULL THEN 'compliant' WHEN @@global.secure_file_priv = '' THEN 'empty' ELSE 'compliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set secure_file_priv = /data/tdsql/secure/ (or NULL when import/export is not needed) in the [mysqld] section of my.cnf / the parameter template and restart the instance.

title: Ensure Symbolic Links Are Disabled
description: MySQL's symbolic links feature allows placing a table's data and index files in directories outside datadir. When enabled, it can be abused for filesystem-level attacks. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure Symbolic Links Are Disabled

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.have_symlink" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Add skip-symbolic-links = 1 to the [mysqld] section of my.cnf / the parameter template and restart the instance.

title: Ensure the `daemon_memcached` Plugin Is Disabled
description: The daemon_memcached plugin allows direct access to InnoDB tables via the Memcached protocol, bypassing SQL-layer privilege checks. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.6 Ensure the `daemon_memcached` Plugin Is Disabled

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.plugins WHERE PLUGIN_NAME = 'daemon_memcached'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: UNINSTALL PLUGIN daemon_memcached;

title: Ensure `default_password_lifetime` Is Reasonably Set
description: default_password_lifetime controls the global default password expiration (in days) for MySQL accounts. A value of 0 means passwords never expire. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Passes when default_password_lifetime is greater than 0 (90 days or less is recommended).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.7 Ensure `default_password_lifetime` Is Reasonably Set

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT CASE WHEN @@global.default_password_lifetime > 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'never expires' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: SET GLOBAL default_password_lifetime = 90; or set the instance parameter through the OSS management platform.

title: Ensure High-Risk Parameters Cannot Be Arbitrarily Modified via `SET GLOBAL`
description: Users with the SUPER or SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN privilege can modify system variables online via SET GLOBAL, including security-related parameters (such as sql_mode, read_only).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.8 Ensure High-Risk Parameters Cannot Be Arbitrarily Modified via `SET GLOBAL`

audit.command: Run SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE Super_priv = 'Y' AND User NOT LIKE 'tdsqlsys%'; and check SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN grants (SELECT * FROM mysql.global_grants WHERE PRIV = 'SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN'). Only TDSQL system accounts may hold them; with audit logging enabled, review the audit trail for unexpected SET GLOBAL statements.

remediation.command: 1. Allow only TDSQL system accounts (tdsqlsys_*) to hold the SUPER privilege. 2. Have business accounts modify parameters uniformly through the OSS management interface. 3. Enable audit logging of SET GLOBAL operations.

title: Ensure Gateway-Layer Secure SQL Protection Is Enabled
description: gateway.security.reject. nowhere 1 Reject DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE gateway.security.reject. nopk 1 Reject CREATE TABLE without a primary key gateway.security.name.re strict 1 Restrict object names to alphanumerics and underscore gateway.security.unsafe_ sysfunc.openflag 1 Intercept unsafe system functions gateway.security.conn.co nn_limit >0 Set a reasonable connection limit Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.9 Ensure Gateway-Layer Secure SQL Protection Is Enabled

audit.command: In the OSS management platform (or the Gateway proxy.json) confirm gateway.security.reject.nowhere = 1, gateway.security.reject.nopk = 1, gateway.security.name.restrict = 1 and gateway.security.unsafe_sysfunc.openflag = 1 for every instance. Any value of 0 is a finding.

remediation.command: Modify the Gateway parameters via the OSS management platform: Parameter Recomm ended

title: Ensure `binlog_format` Is Set to `ROW`
description: The binlog format determines how the binary log records changes. The ROW format records row-level data changes, whereas the STATEMENT format records the original SQL statements. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.10 Ensure `binlog_format` Is Set to `ROW`

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.binlog_format" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL binlog_format = 'ROW'; through the OSS management platform (no restart required) and persist it in the parameter template.

title: Ensure the TXSQL SQL Firewall Is Enabled
description: The TXSQL kernel includes a built-in SQL firewall (txsql_sql_filter) that can reject specific SQL types/keyword patterns or limit the concurrent connections matching a rule. Rule metadata is stored in information_schema.txsql_sql_filter_info (fields: TYPE, ITEM_ID, CURRENT_CONN, MAX_CONN, REJECTED_SQL_COUNT, CREATED_TIME, EXPIRE_TIME, EXPIRED, KEY_STR, ORIGIN_STR, etc.).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.11 Ensure the TXSQL SQL Firewall Is Enabled

audit.command: -- Check the SQL firewall switch SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'txsql_sql_filter_enable'; -- View configured filter rules and their hit/reject statistics SELECT * FROM information_schema.txsql_sql_filter_info; Confirm txsql_sql_filter_enable = ON, and that interception rules are configured for critical scenarios (financial transaction tables, user data tables).

remediation.command: Configuring rules through the OSS management interface is recommended (OSS validates rule legality before pushing). If executing SQL directly as an administrator, the rule syntax of the txsql_sql_filter variable is: -- Enable the SQL firewall SET GLOBAL txsql_sql_filter_enable = ON;

title: Ensure Connection-Control Failed-Login Delay Is Enabled
description: TDSQL MySQL instances integrate the upstream connection_control plugin (SQLEngine/plugin/connection_control/connection_control.cc), which imposes an increasing delay on a client connection after consecutive failed logins, mitigating brute-force attacks. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Passes when the CONNECTION_CONTROL plugin is ACTIVE and connection_control_failed_connections_threshold is greater than 0; review the min/max connection delays against policy.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.12 Ensure Connection-Control Failed-Login Delay Is Enabled

audit.command: pl=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.plugins WHERE PLUGIN_NAME = 'CONNECTION_CONTROL' AND PLUGIN_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; th=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.connection_control_failed_connections_threshold" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ "$pl" -ge 1 ] && [ "$th" -gt 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: INSTALL PLUGIN CONNECTION_CONTROL SONAME 'connection_control.so'; INSTALL PLUGIN CONNECTION_CONTROL_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS SONAME 'connection_control.so'; SET GLOBAL connection_control_failed_connections_threshold = 3; and set connection_control_min/max_connection_delay per policy.

title: Ensure Primary Keys Are Enforced and MyISAM Engine Is Prohibited
description: TXSQL enforces "mandatory primary keys" and an "engine allowlist" through two kernel parameters plus Gateway-layer supplementation: sql_require_primary_key (MySQL 8.0 upstream) - a primary key is required when creating/altering tables reject_table_no_pk (TXSQL enhancement) - reject DML on tables without a primary key reject_create_table_myisam (TXSQL enhancement) - reject creation of MyISAM tables ... Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5). Passes when sql_require_primary_key, reject_table_no_pk and reject_create_table_myisam all exist and are ON; also run the benchmark query to find existing tables without a primary key or using MyISAM.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.14 Ensure Primary Keys Are Enforced and MyISAM Engine Is Prohibited

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('sql_require_primary_key', 'reject_table_no_pk', 'reject_create_table_myisam')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 2 {n++; v = toupper($2); if (v == "ON" || v == "1") ok++} END {print (n == 3 && ok == 3) ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}'

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL sql_require_primary_key = ON; SET GLOBAL reject_table_no_pk = ON; SET GLOBAL reject_create_table_myisam = ON; persist them in the parameter template and add primary keys / convert MyISAM tables to InnoDB.

title: Ensure System Account Privileges Are Minimized
description: TDSQL includes several built-in system accounts for different purposes. Each account should hold only the minimum privileges necessary for its function.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure System Account Privileges Are Minimized

audit.command: Run SHOW GRANTS FOR 'tdsqlsys_check'@'%'; SHOW GRANTS FOR 'tdsqlsys_agent'@'%'; SHOW GRANTS FOR 'tdsqlsys_repl'@'%'; (and the other tdsqlsys_* accounts) and compare each with the minimum privileges required for its function per the benchmark table (e.g. tdsqlsys_repl only REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT). Any extra privilege is a finding.

remediation.command: Adjust system account privileges through the TDSQL Manager to ensure each account holds only the necessary privileges. Note: Modifying system account privileges may affect normal operation of TDSQL components; test thoroughly before making changes.

title: Ensure No Excessive `PROCESS` Privilege Grants
description: The PROCESS privilege allows users to view the current queries of all threads and users (SHOW PROCESSLIST), potentially exposing sensitive data contained in other users' SQL statements.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.7 Ensure No Excessive `PROCESS` Privilege Grants

audit.command: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE Process_priv = 'Y' AND User NOT LIKE 'tdsqlsys%'; Confirm only system accounts and approved administrators hold this privilege.

remediation.command: REVOKE PROCESS ON *.* FROM 'username'@'host';

title: Ensure the OSS API Allowlist Is Configured
description: TDSQL OSS supports an IP allowlist for API callers, restricting management API access to specific IP addresses.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.10 Ensure the OSS API Allowlist Is Configured

audit.command: Check the allowlist configuration in scheduler.xml: <whitelist ip="..." .../> Confirm the ip field is not empty.

remediation.command: Configure the allowlist IP list (allowing only the management/operations subnets): <whitelist ip="10.0.1.0/24;10.0.2.100" .../>

title: Ensure `log_raw` Is Disabled
description: The log_raw parameter controls whether passwords are recorded in cleartext in the logs. When enabled, passwords in statements such as CHANGE MASTER, CREATE USER, and GRANT are written to the logs in cleartext. Runs the mysql client against the TDSQL data node selected by TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS (e.g. "-h10.0.0.5 -P4001 -utdsql_audit"); keep the password in ~/.my.cnf or a login path rather than MYSQL_PWD or the command line (see 1.4 and 1.5).
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4 Ensure `log_raw` Is Disabled

audit.command: out=$(mysql ${TDSQL_MYSQL_OPTS:-} -NBe "SELECT @@global.log_raw" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Ensure log_raw = OFF in the [mysqld] section of my.cnf / the parameter template (SET GLOBAL log_raw = OFF).

title: Ensure OSS Management Operations Are Audited
description: The TDSQL OSS management plane records write-type administrative operations independently of database SQL auditing. This audit trail must be available and retained for instance lifecycle actions, configuration changes, and account or privilege changes.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.6 Ensure OSS Management Operations Are Audited

audit.command: 1. Confirm in the TDSQL management platform that the OSS audit database is configured and healthy. 2. Identify a recent non-destructive write-type management operation, such as an approved parameter-template update. 3. Confirm that it appears in the OSS audit view or database with operator, source, action, timestamp, result, and target object. 4. Confirm that OSS records are included in centralized collection and retention. Do not use query_interfaces_logged_in_audit as the test for this recommendation; that setting controls query-interface auditing and is assessed in 6.10.

remediation.command: Configure or repair the OSS audit database through the supported TDSQL management procedure. Verify that write-type operations generate records, protect the audit- database credentials as described in 2.7, and include OSS records in the centralized collection defined in 6.8.

title: Ensure a Reasonable Log Retention Policy
description: Each TDSQL component has a log cleanup mechanism; ensure log retention meets security audit and compliance requirements.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.7 Ensure a Reasonable Log Retention Policy

audit.command: Review retention settings: OSS scheduler.xml log_clean.max_save_days (default 30) and log_clean.max_size (100 GB); Manager scheduler.xml clear_log.resv_capacity (20 GB); Gateway proxy.json gateway.log.clean.time (14 days) and gateway.log.clean.size (10 GB). Values must meet the retention requirement (typically at least 90 days, 180+ in finance); shorter retention is a finding.

remediation.command: Adjust the retention parameters according to compliance requirements (typically at least 90 days; the finance industry may require 180 days or more). Recommendations: 1. Increase max_save_days to meet compliance requirements. 2. Forward logs to a centralized log platform (SIEM), keeping only recent logs locally. 3. Ensure sufficient disk space to support the retention requirement.

title: Ensure Centralized Audit Log Collection Is Configured
description: TDSQL can use managed Filebeat instances to collect logs from compute nodes, data nodes, and Agents and send them to Kafka or Elasticsearch. The destination may be DBbrain full-link audit analysis or an equivalent enterprise SIEM. Central collection must cover all production instances and all security-relevant log sources.
reference: CIS Tencent TDSQL 10.3.22 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.8 Ensure Centralized Audit Log Collection Is Configured
